column1: # Why measures: a first-order continuous-time delta-sigma modulator clocked at
# 5 MHz over 5 us. RSpice reproduces the reference bitstream exactly — all 24
# transitions of v(xmod.adffq), same order, same directions, none missing or
# added, including the two the reference itself skips. What the pointwise gate
# trips on is where the edges land, and there the deck-step reference is the
# one that has not converged. Refining ngspice-46's own step 10x collapses its
# transitions onto an exact 104.8500 + n*200 ns lattice, and RSpice is already
# on an exact 104.8000 + n*200 ns lattice — 50 ps away, uniformly. The
#   crossing        deck-step ref    refined ref      RSpice
# Over all 24 edges the reference moves by up to 823 ps under its own
# refinement, and RSpice sits up to 873 ps from the deck-step reference but
# only 50 ps from the refined one. The analog side has the same shape, with
# RSpice closer to the refined reference than the deck-step reference is in
#   measure                     deck-step ref   refined ref   RSpice
# Sources: 13 kHz 0.3 V input, 5 MHz clock, .tran 0.01u over 5 us.
# v(xmod.adffq) is the modulator bitstream at +/-1; v(xmod.outintp) and
# v(xmod.outintn) are the differential integrator outputs. Tolerances are
# twice the larger of the reference's refinement movement and RSpice's
# The crossing gates carry the bitstream: an n-th crossing only lands within
# 2 ns of the reference if every decision before it matched, since a single
# flipped bit moves it by a whole 200 ns clock.
